heroHeadline: Homan: 570,000 Deportations Since Inauguration — Senate Reconciliation Floor Vote Set for May 18; OIDO Watchdog Closed; 11th Circuit Bars Mandatory No-Bond Detention
heroSubtitle: Border Czar Tom Homan disclosed approximately 570,000 total deportations since Trump's inauguration on January 20, 2025 (through early May 2026) and declared 'mass deportations are coming' as he pushed back against MAGA critics demanding faster enforcement (NPR, May 7). ICE separately disclosed 16,368 removals from the San Diego region alone in the first 71 days of the administration — 66% Mexican nationals. The Senate reconciliation package allocating $71.7 billion for ICE and CBP (ICE: ~$38.2B) is scheduled for a Senate floor vote the week of May 18, with Trump's June 1 signing deadline looming. On May 5, DHS shut down the Office of Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO) — the independent watchdog Congress created in the 2019 NDAA to investigate ICE detention deaths — citing a disputed 'defunding' interpretation experts say lacks legal basis. The closure eliminates the only independent oversight of a system with 30+ FY2026 custody deaths. On May 6, the 11th Circuit struck down Trump's mandatory no-bond detention policy, the second appeals court to do so, creating a four-circuit split requiring bond hearings for ICE detainees in Florida, Georgia, and Alabama and making Supreme Court review near-certain. Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons remains in post until his May 31 resignation; no successor has been named. The DHS 287(g) program stands at 1,784 active MOAs covering 39 states.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, court records, and Congressional records
